root_cause_analysis.symptom: Cycle-6 close-report verdict NO on §5.3.D bullet 5: final_summary text is missing from the merged subagent lifecycle card in real Codex production sessions, despite cycle-6 fixture-based QA passing.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: Cycle-6 dev hallucinated the field names message.final_summary and message.finalSummary on close_agent events. The real Codex protocol carries final-summary text on a different shape — event.agentsStates: { [threadId]: { status, message }} — surfaced primarily on wait_agent end (per Codex TUI's wait_complete_lines at multi_agents.rs:495-535,559-586). Additionally, runCodex.ts never persists subagentLifecycles state across mapper invocations, so even a corrected mapper would emit nothing in production because the buffer Map vanishes between events.

root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: All production reads return undefined → renderer's result.final_summary chain falls through to placeholder → user-visible card shows no summary. Cycle-6 fixture tests passed because the fixture itself carried the hallucinated shape, masking the gap.

novelty_check.rationale: Cycle 6 worked at L3 (defining a synthetic envelope shape + view rendering) and got the data field name wrong. Cycle 7 works at L4 (cross-component data flow): the bridge MUST forward the correct field, the orchestrator MUST persist the lifecycle state map across invocations, and the mapper MUST read the real protocol path. Although L4 has been touched before (cycle 6's mapper close-branch is L4-ish wiring), the distinguishing factor of THIS attempt is reference_source.tier — cycle 6 used hand-rolled field names (effectively tier_3_tainted), this cycle uses Codex CLI v0.125.0 ts-rs type definitions verbatim (tier_1_external). The novelty is anchored at the reference-integrity dimension, not just at a layer-shift. Per Contract D layer-differentiation, cycle 7 also adds a new wiring dimension (orchestrator state plumbing) that cycle 6 missed — codex adversarial review specifically discovered this third-layer gap. Both factors together (correct reference + new wiring layer) make this attempt meaningfully distinct.
